lessons.title: What Makes Someone Brave?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe what being brave means.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss favourite superheroes and what makes them brave.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss that being brave isn't about superpowers, but about trying new things even when nervous, using examples.
key_questions: Do you have to have superpowers to be brave?

differentiation.extension: Give own example of everyday bravery

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of bravery as an everyday quality — evidence for PSED.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap what being brave really means.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a time you or a family member was brave.

lessons.title: Describing My Superpower
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe an imaginary superpower using full sentences.
lessons.main_activity: Children imagine and describe their own superpower to a partner using full sentences.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note imaginative language and sentence construction — evidence for CL.2.
lessons.home_link: Talk about what superpower you'd like to have with family.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'Supertato' or a Superhero Story
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how the hero solved the problem.
lessons.main_activity: Read a superhero-themed story, discussing how the hero bravely solved the problem.
key_questions: What problem did the hero face?
How did they solve it bravely?

differentiation.extension: Explain the hero's bravery in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension of problem-solving and bravery themes — evidence for LIT.1/PSED.1.
lessons.plenary: Discuss favourite part of the story.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Being Brave About Year 1
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name one thing they feel brave/excited about for Year 1.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children know about Year 1 so far.
lessons.main_activity: Children share what excites them and what feels a little scary about moving to Year 1, normalising mixed feelings.
key_questions: What are you excited about for Year 1?
Is there anything that feels a bit scary?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note emotional processing of transition — evidence for PSED.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap that it's normal to feel both excited and nervous.
lessons.home_link: Talk about Year 1 with your family.

lessons.title: Listening to a Year 1 Teacher/Visitor
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to listen attentively and ask a question about Year 1.
lessons.starter_activity: Prepare a question to ask about Year 1.
lessons.main_activity: (If possible) a Year 1 teacher visits to talk about their classroom; children listen and ask prepared questions. If unavailable, discuss using photos/information instead.
key_questions: What did you learn about Year 1?

differentiation.support: Adult asks the question on child's behalf
differentiation.extension: Child asks their own follow-up question

lessons.assessment_notes: Note listening attention and question-forming — evidence for CL.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap what was learned about Year 1.
lessons.home_link: Think of another question about Year 1 to ask at home.

lessons.title: Writing About My Superpower
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write a sentence about their imaginary superpower.
lessons.main_activity: Children draw themselves as a superhero and attempt to write about their superpower using known phonics sounds.

differentiation.extension: Independent phonetic attempt at a short sentence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note writing progress and imaginative expression — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share superhero writing with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Draw yourself as a superhero together at home.

lessons.title: New Independence Skills for Year 1
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to practise a new independence skill needed for Year 1.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss skills that might be needed more in Year 1 (packing a bag, opening lunch containers).
lessons.main_activity: Practise a chosen independence skill (e.g. opening a snack wrapper, putting on a jumper) with encouragement.
resources_needed: Real items to practise with (wrappers, jumpers, zips)
lessons.assessment_notes: Note growing independence in preparation for Year 1 — evidence for PSED.2.
lessons.home_link: Practise an independence skill at home this week.

lessons.title: Talking About What I'm Looking Forward To
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain what they're looking forward to using 'because'.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult models: 'I'm looking forward to summer because it's warm.'
lessons.main_activity: Children complete and share 'I'm looking forward to Year 1 because ___' sentences.
key_questions: What are you looking forward to?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note causal language use and positive transition talk — evidence for CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Class list of things to look forward to.
lessons.home_link: Share what you're looking forward to with your family.

lessons.title: Retelling the Superhero Story
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell the story's key events in sequence.
lessons.main_activity: Using picture cards, children retell the story sequence using sequencing words.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sequencing and retelling ability — evidence for LIT.1/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One group retells to the class.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Being a Superhero Friend
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a kind/brave action a friend could do to help someone.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss that everyday kindness can be 'heroic'.
lessons.main_activity: Children think of a kind or brave action they could do for a friend (like a real-life superhero), and try to do it today.
key_questions: What kind/brave thing could you do today?
How did it feel to help?

differentiation.support: Adult suggests an action to try
differentiation.extension: Child identifies and performs their own action

lessons.assessment_notes: Note prosocial behaviour and self-initiated kindness — evidence for PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Award 'Everyday Hero' recognition for kind actions seen today.
lessons.home_link: Be an 'everyday hero' for someone at home today.

lessons.title: Following Instructions: Superhero Training Course
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to follow multi-step instructions in a fun physical challenge.
lessons.main_activity: Set up a 'superhero training' obstacle course; give 2-3 step instructions for children to follow in sequence.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note instruction-following capacity — evidence for CL.1.
lessons.home_link: Practise following instructions for a fun challenge at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Superhero Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read simple superhero-themed words.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations reading superhero-themed word cards and simple sentences (e.g. 'the hero can fly').

differentiation.support: Read simple CVC words with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application to themed vocabulary — evidence for LIT.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading superhero words over the week.

lessons.title: Feeling Ready and Brave for Year 1
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to express feeling more confident about Year 1 after this week's learning.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's learning about bravery and Year 1.
lessons.main_activity: Children reflect on how they feel about Year 1 now compared to the start of the week, sharing with the group.
key_questions: How do you feel about Year 1 now?
What has helped you feel more ready?

differentiation.extension: Explain the change in feeling with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note emotional processing progress across the week — evidence for PSED.1.
lessons.plenary: Class cheer: 'We are ready and brave for Year 1!'
lessons.home_link: Share how you feel about Year 1 with your family.

lessons.title: Superheroes and Bravery Quiz Game
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer recall questions about bravery and Year 1 learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Quiz-style game asking questions about bravery, kindness, and Year 1 from the week.
key_questions: What does it mean to be brave?
What is one thing you're looking forward to in Year 1?
lessons.assessment_notes: Assess recall and comprehension — evidence for CL.1.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on what you've learned this week.

lessons.title: Phonics Review: Superhero Reading Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read superhero-themed sentences fluently.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations reading a range of superhero-themed sentences with increasing fluency, celebrating overall progress.
key_questions: Can you read it more quickly?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note reading fluency progress — evidence for LIT.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading superhero sentences over the weekend.
